name: RNAGym leaderboard against Wang et al. 2026 on RNAErnie and AIDO.RNA: explained by a non-comparable RNAErnie score
description: Review of discrepancy-055eb0dd61040574, revision 3: explained. Discrepancy rules version 4 gave discrepancy-8c69346a6089882b a new ID (two-study-conflict); the state and resolution are carried forward unchanged.

attributes.rationale: Both sides score the same 31 RNAGym ncRNA assays (26 ribozyme, 3 tRNA, 2 aptamer, all at most 425 nt, so Wang's 440 nt filter keeps every one). The order differs because the v0.1.1 leaderboard's RNAErnie score is not comparable with its AIDO.RNA score. The RNAGym maintainers later stated that RNAErnie's scorer takes one pass over the unmasked wild type, a softmax rather than a log-softmax, and sums raw probability differences at the mutated positions, so its 0.1937 is 'not comparable with the masked checkpoints' (commit d43db8c613); it was carried over unverified because it needs a paddlepaddle environment. At v0.1.1 AIDO.RNA was scored with mut-fill, the weakest of four fill strategies; rescored with wt-fill it 'takes second place from RNA-ERNIE' (commit d024cd81a3). The v0.2 leaderboard ranks AIDO.RNA 650M (0.21) and 1.6B (0.20) above RNA-ERNIE (0.19), the order Wang reports. RNA-ERNIE's ribozyme lead (0.14) falls to about 0.02 within a mutation count, and mutation count alone scores 0.20 on ribozymes, so its lead mostly reflects how many mutations a variant has. Wang's SR is the absolute Spearman (Methods), which RNAGym's own script also reported until commit ac371bff28; its effect on this pair cannot be measured without per-assay predictions, and it is not needed to explain the reversal.

name: ProteinBench against ProteinGym on ESM-IF1 and ProteinMPNN: different tasks
description: Review of discrepancy-1f1fd7fb7ee75052, revision 2: explained. Discrepancy rules version 4 gave discrepancy-d734930095432234 a new ID (two-study-conflict); the state and resolution are carried forward unchanged.

attributes.rationale: ProteinBench measures sequence design on de novo backbones of length 100 to 500, scored by pLDDT and scTM after refolding, the task ProteinMPNN was built for. Every consensus comparison is ProteinGym zero-shot variant effect prediction (DMS Spearman, clinical AUC), where ESM-IF1 scores 0.422 against ProteinMPNN's 0.257. Design quality and variant scoring are different endpoints; both sets of results are kept as reported. The high severity comes from the strong-consensus step cancelling the cross-task step (issue 201).

name: PFMBench against ProteinGym on ESM-2 and ESM3: ProteinGym zero-shot scores differ

attributes.rationale: Eleven of PFMBench's twelve comparisons are supervised probing tasks with no counterpart elsewhere. The twelfth, PFMBench's ProteinGym zero-shot row, gives ESM3 0.414 and ESM-2 0.439, while ProteinGym's own files give ESM3 open 1.4B 0.466 and ESM-2 650M 0.414. Being checked: PFMBench's assay subset, scoring rule and checkpoints (issue 210).
